environmentalPersistence: High — soil half-life 60–100 days; persists in groundwater; one of the most detected pesticides in US water supplies

morphologicalEffects.heightSuppression: Strong — photosynthesis inhibition starves plant of energy for growth
morphologicalEffects.wilting: Moderate-strong — energy deprivation from photosynthesis block
morphologicalEffects.chlorosis: Very strong — PSII inhibition causes bleaching; most prominent visual symptom. Characteristic interveinal chlorosis progressing to uniform bleaching.
morphologicalEffects.necrosis: Moderate-strong — chlorotic tissue dies as energy starvation progresses
morphologicalEffects.pigmentation: Minimal — photosynthetic energy needed for anthocyanin synthesis is cut off
morphologicalEffects.newVsOldLeaves: Chlorosis appears uniformly across all leaves; new growth most affected

physiologyEffects.chlorophyllReduction: Very strong — direct PSII inhibition causes chlorophyll bleaching; 70–95% at effective doses
physiologyEffects.photosyntheticRate: Near-zero at effective doses — atrazine's primary mechanism is photosystem II electron transport block
physiologyEffects.stomatalConductance: Moderately reduced — secondary to photosynthesis block

molecularEffects.oxidativeStress: Strong — blocked electron transport in PSII causes electron leakage and ROS generation
molecularEffects.lipidPeroxidation: Strong — particularly thylakoid membrane lipid peroxidation

microbiomeEffects.beneficialBacteriaEffect: Strongly suppressed; atrazine-degrading Pseudomonas strains may persist
microbiomeEffects.fungalEffect: Mycorrhizal associations disrupted; some atrazine-degrading fungi increase

temporalDynamics.recoveryTime: None at effective doses; sub-lethal doses may allow slow recovery

visualSimulation.colorChanges: Green → interveinal yellow-green → uniform yellow → white bleaching → brown necrosis
visualSimulation.firstAffectedRegion: Interveinal mesophyll — PSII is located in mesophyll chloroplasts
visualSimulation.damageSpread: Uniform across leaf surface — PSII block is ubiquitous
visualSimulation.damagePattern: Progressive bleaching — from yellow to white to brown — is the most visually distinctive herbicide pattern in the simulator
visualSimulation.heatmapGlow: Strong bleached signal — chlorophyllide degradation products give distinctive signature; near-zero anthocyanin
visualSimulation.microbiomeParticles: Strongly reduced; elevated pathogen fraction; resistome elevated

synergies.synergyNote: Glyphosate + atrazine combination addresses both amino acid synthesis and photosynthesis simultaneously — used in combination weed control programs

educationalContext.realWorldSources: Agricultural runoff — most commonly detected pesticide in US groundwater and surface water; applied to ~70% of US corn acres annually
educationalContext.classification: Photosystem II inhibiting herbicide / endocrine disruptor
educationalContext.agriculturalUse: Pre-emergent and post-emergent weed control in corn, sorghum, sugarcane — ~80 million lbs/year applied in US alone
educationalContext.humanToxicity: Moderate — banned in EU since 2004; endocrine disruption concerns; linked to Parkinson's disease in agricultural workers; frogs show sex reversal at extremely low concentrations
educationalContext.climateLink: Atrazine in water bodies disrupts aquatic endocrine systems — climate-driven altered water cycles may concentrate atrazine in drought-reduced waterways
educationalContext.indoorOutdoor: Outdoor — agricultural; detected in tap water in agricultural regions
educationalContext.whyStudentsCare: Banned in Europe but legal and widely used in the US — a direct example of different risk standards across countries. The frog sex reversal story (Tyrone Hayes/UC Berkeley research) is one of the most compelling science-policy stories in modern environmental science.
educationalContext.realWorldIssue: Groundwater contamination, EU vs US pesticide policy, endocrine disruption, frog population collapse
